title: Maryland v. Buie (1990)
key_points: Holding: During an in-home arrest, officers may make a quick protective sweep of spaces adjoining the arrest location, and of other areas if they have reasonable suspicion someone dangerous is there.
officer_notes: Scenario: Arresting a robbery suspect in his basement, you glance into the adjoining room where a partner could hide.
Takeaway: A sweep is a cursory visual check for people, not a search for evidence.
